mobile.reason: No patched release exists: the advisory marks <=2.0.2 vulnerable and 2.0.2 is the newest version published. image-size is a build-time dependency of metro (the React Native bundler) and only ever parses this repository's own committed image assets — attacker-supplied ICNS files never reach it, so the DoS has no exposed surface here. Remove this entry as soon as image-size ships a fix and the expo/metro chain picks it up.

Same situation and same surface as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr: no patched release exists (<=2.0.2 vulnerable, 2.0.2 is the latest), and the JXL/HEIF parse only runs at build time over first-party assets. Remove when upstream ships a fix.

A patched release EXISTS (0.5.0) but cannot be installed here, which is why this entry reads differently from the image-size ones above. decode-uri-component 0.5.0 is ESM-only ("type": "module", one default export), and its only consumer in this tree is query-string 7.1.3, which is CommonJS and does require("decode-uri-component")(value). expo-router 56 pins query-string ^7.1.3 — 56.2.20, the newest 56, still does — and its compiled CJS requires query-string in four navigation modules, so neither the patch nor a jump to query-string 9 (ESM-only as well) is reachable without breaking deep links. Measured, not assumed: with the override in place the jest suite dies with "SyntaxError: Unexpected token export" inside query-string/index.js, and running 0.5.0 through this project's own babel-preset-expo — what Metro does to node_modules — yields module.exports = { default }, so query-string's call site throws "is not a function". The exposed surface is a malformed percent-encoded deep link hanging the app's own JS thread on the tablet that opened it; no server and no other user is reachable from it. Remove this entry as soon as expo-router accepts a query-string that takes a patched decode-uri-component.
